name: Long-Wheelbase Era
description:
Unveiled at the Frankfurt Motor Show on 15 September 2011, the 991 was only the third all-new 911 platform since 1963 and, in Porsche's own words, the greatest engineering leap in the model's history: close to 90 per cent of its components were new or substantially redeveloped. The wheelbase grew by 100 mm (3.9 in) to 2,450 mm (96.5 in), the rear axle moved 76 mm (3.0 in) further back for better weight distribution, and an aluminium-steel body cut around 80 kg (176 lb) compared with the 997 despite extra equipment. It introduced the world's first seven-speed manual gearbox, and from the 2013 Turbo onwards offered active aerodynamics and rear-axle steering.

The naturally aspirated 991.1 phase (2011–2015) ran a 3.4-litre Carrera with 350 PS (257 kW; 345 hp) and a 3.8-litre Carrera S with 400 PS (294 kW; 395 hp), later joined by the wide-body Carrera 4/4S, the return of the Targa with its 19-second automatic roof (2014), the GTS (2014), a 520 PS Turbo, and the GT3, GT3 RS and 911 R — a 500 PS manual weighing 1,370 kg (3,020 lb), built 991 times. The 50th Anniversary Edition marked half a century with exactly 1,963 cars.

The 991.2 facelift, shown at the 2015 Frankfurt show, brought twin turbocharging to every Carrera: a three-litre flat-six developing 370, 420 and 450 PS across Carrera, S and GTS. That phase added the purist Carrera T, the wingless GT3 Touring, a 520 PS GT3 RS, the 700 PS GT2 RS (6:47.3 on the Nordschleife), a 607 PS Turbo S Exclusive Series, the 77-car track-only 935 and, last of all, the 1,948-unit Speedster. The final 991 left Zuffenhausen on 20 December 2019 after 233,540 units — the best-selling 911 generation — and the millionth 911 of any type was itself a 991 Carrera S.

variants.description: The 911 Carrera opened the third all-new 911 platform in 2011 with a naturally aspirated 3.4-litre flat-six of 350 PS (257 kW; 345 hp) and 390 Nm (288 lb-ft), paired with the world's first seven-speed manual or an optional seven-speed PDK; it needed 4.6 s (PDK) to 100 km/h and reached 287 km/h (178 mph). The 2016 facelift (991.2) replaced that engine with a 3.0-litre twin-turbo six of 370 PS (272 kW; 365 hp) and 450 Nm (332 lb-ft), cutting the sprint to 4.4 s while using about 12 per cent less fuel. Coupé and Cabriolet, rear-wheel drive, with PASM and rear-axle steering optional. Figures shown are 991.2 specification.

variants.description: The Carrera S has long been the 911's sweet spot, and the 991 carried that across two engines. variants.description: The all-wheel-drive Carrera 4 arrived at the Paris Motor Show in September 2012, adding PTM multi-plate traction to the wide-body 991 shell. It shares its engines with the rear-drive car: 350 PS (345 hp) from the 3.4-litre naturally aspirated six to 2015, then 370 PS (365 hp) and 450 Nm (332 lb-ft) from the 3.0-litre twin-turbo. PASM lowered suspension became standard with the facelift, and rear-axle steering was added as an option. The 991.2 Coupé with PDK runs to 100 km/h in 4.3 s (4.1 s with Sport Chrono), carries 290 km/h (180 mph) and weighs 1,500 kg (3,307 lb) in DIN trim.

variants.name: 911 Carrera T
variants.drivetrain: Rear-wheel drive with mechanical rear differential lock
variants.description: Launched in October 2017, the Carrera T — T for Touring — revives the purist brief of the 1968 911 T. It takes the base 3.0-litre twin-turbo with 370 PS (272 kW; 365 hp) and 450 Nm (332 lb-ft), adds a shorter final drive, a mechanical rear differential lock, PASM sports suspension dropped 20 mm, a weight-optimised Sport Chrono package, a shortened red-pattern shift lever and Sport-Tex seats. Weight falls to 1,425 kg (3,142 lb) — 20 kg below a comparable Carrera — through lighter glass, door pull loops, reduced sound deadening and deleted rear seats and PCM, both refittable free of charge. Rear-axle steering and PDK were optional.

variants.description: Since 1975 the Turbo has been the 911's technology flagship, and the 991 made it faster and far more usable. The 2013 car introduced a 3.8-litre twin-turbo six with variable turbine geometry, 520 PS (382 kW; 513 hp) and 660 Nm (487 lb-ft), plus the first active aerodynamics on a series 911 and standard rear-axle steering. For 2016 the engine grew to 540 PS (397 kW; 533 hp), with 710 Nm (524 lb-ft) available on overboost. PTM all-wheel drive and a seven-speed PDK are fixed; the facelift coupé sprints to 100 km/h in 2.9 s, reaches 320 km/h (199 mph) and weighs 1,595 kg (3,516 lb).

Rear-axle steering, PTV Plus, dynamic engine mounts and centre-lock wheels carry over. Zero to 100 km/h takes 3.9 s, top speed is 316 km/h (196 mph) and kerb weight 1,413 kg (3,115 lb) — the name echoes the 1973 Carrera RS 2.7 Touring.

The 991.1 car (Geneva 2015) used a 4.0-litre flat-six with 500 PS (368 kW; 493 hp) and 460 Nm (339 lb-ft), Turbo-style rear-fender intakes, fender louvres, a magnesium roof, bucket seats based on the 918 Spyder's and PDK only: 0–100 km/h in 3.3 s, 315 km/h (196 mph), 1,420 kg (3,131 lb). variants.name: 911 GT2 RS
variants.description: Unveiled at the 2017 Goodwood Festival of Speed, the GT2 RS was the most powerful production 911 yet: 700 PS (515 kW; 690 hp) and 750 Nm (553 lb-ft) from a 3.8-litre twin-turbo six, driven through a seven-speed PDK to the rear wheels only. It covers 0–100 km/h in 2.8 s, reaches 340 km/h (211 mph) and weighs 1,470 kg (3,241 lb) — about 2.1 kg per horsepower. The optional Weissach package saves a further 30 kg with carbon and magnesium parts, including braided carbon wheels. On 27 September 2017 a production car lapped the Nürburgring Nordschleife in 6:47.3, then the fastest-ever by a road-legal Porsche.

variants.description: The 911 R is the 991's purist statement: GT3 RS mechanicals stripped of wing, roll cage and aero clutter. Its 4.0-litre naturally aspirated flat-six makes 500 PS (368 kW; 493 hp) and 460 Nm (339 lb-ft), revs to 9,000 rpm and drives the rear wheels through a six-speed manual with a short-throw lever. At 1,370 kg (3,020 lb) it was the lightest 911 of its era, needing 3.8 s to 100 km/h and running to 323 km/h (201 mph) — quicker than the winged RS because of lower drag. Carbon buckets with Pepita cloth, pull-strap door releases, PCCB ceramics and a numbered aluminium badge mark each of the 991 cars built for 2016.

variants.name: 911 Speedster
variants.description: The final 991 and the last of the run. Shown as a concept for Porsche's 70th anniversary in 2018 and confirmed for production that October, the Speedster went on sale in May 2019 on the GT3's chassis with a shortened double-bubble roof, a Carrera 4 Cabriolet shell and a central fuel cap. Its 4.0-litre naturally aspirated flat-six develops 510 PS (375 kW; 503 hp) at 8,400 rpm and 470 Nm (347 lb-ft), revving to 9,000 rpm, and drives a six-speed manual with a titanium exhaust lighter than the standard system. PCCB brakes are standard; a Heritage Design package is optional. Exactly 1,948 were built, the last leaving Zuffenhausen on 20 December 2019.

variants.name: 911 50th Anniversary Edition
variants.power: 400 PS (294 kW; 395 hp); 430 PS (316 kW; 424 hp) with Powerkit
variants.description: To mark the 911's 50th birthday Porsche built 1,963 anniversary coupés — one for every year since the 1963 Frankfurt debut — based on the rear-drive Carrera S. The wide Carrera 4S body, 20-inch Fuchs-style wheels, chrome window and grille trim, green instrument dials with white needles and Pepita (houndstooth) seat inserts set it apart, while PASM and PTV were standard. Output was 400 PS (294 kW; 395 hp), rising to 430 PS (424 hp) with the Powerkit, which North American cars received as standard. Porsche quotes 0–100 km/h in 4.5 s (4.3 s with PDK) and 300 km/h (186 mph). Announced in June 2013, shown at the IAA and offered only to existing Porsche owners.

variants.name: Porsche 935
variants.description: The 935 is a track-only homage to the 1978 'Moby Dick' Le Mans racer, unveiled at Rennsport Reunion VI at Laguna Seca in September 2018 with deliveries from June 2019. Based on the 991.2 GT2 RS, it keeps that car's 3.8-litre twin-turbo six with 700 PS (515 kW; 690 hp) and a seven-speed PDK, but replaces nearly every panel with carbon-fibre composite: 4,865 mm long, 2,034 mm wide, with a 1,909 x 400 mm rear wing, 115-litre FIA fuel cell, welded roll cage and Cosworth display. At 1,380 kg (3,042 lb) it is lighter than its donor. Just 77 were built at 701,948 euros plus VAT.

Only 500 coupés were built, each in Golden Yellow Metallic with twin carbon-weave stripes and carbon bonnet, roof, side skirts and adjustable rear wing, plus 20-inch centre-lock wheels with golden highlights and a bespoke leather interior. Unveiled at the 2017 Goodwood Festival of Speed.

variants.name: 911 Turbo GT
variants.description: The 911 Turbo GT is a 991.2-generation Turbo derivative that Porsche never announced in a press release, a model page or a technical data sheet: newsroom.porsche.com carries no Turbo GT article at all (searched 2026-10-03 through the newsroom search index) and Porsche's own archived US technical-specification list jumps from the 2018 911 Carrera T straight to the 2019 Speedster and GT3 RS. There is no Wikipedia article about the car in any language, and Porsche Cars North America never offered it, so there is no US press material or configurator entry either. The car is real — it can be photographed at Klassikstadt Frankfurt — and the widely circulated description is a lightly modified 991.2 Turbo coupé with a 3.8-litre twin-turbo flat-six, 645 PS and either a six-speed manual or the seven-speed PDK, good for 330 km/h. None of those figures could be traced to a fetchable primary source in this session, so every specification field on this record is deliberately null: the variant is published as a disclosed gap rather than as a car with numbers. What it needs next is a citable Porsche specification, not a better-sounding guess.

missing: No primary Porsche source is reachable for this car: newsroom.porsche.com has no 911 Turbo GT article (searched 2026-10-03) and Porsche published no model page or technical data sheet — the launch seems never to have been published on the newsroom, so engine, power, torque, acceleration, top speed, weight, drivetrain and transmission are all null and must not be filled from secondary retellings without a citation

The figures in circulation — 3.8-litre twin-turbo flat-six, 645 PS, 800 Nm, 0–100 km/h 2.9 s, 330 km/h, six-speed manual or seven-speed PDK, model year 2018 — come from secondary retellings only and are recorded here as context, not as data; the '2018' model year itself is unconfirmed against Porsche
Production total unknown: Porsche published no run length for the Turbo GT and Porsche Cars North America never offered the car, so no US press material exists to triangulate a number

Porsche quoted 217,930 991s built to 31 October 2018; the final count is 233,540 (20 December 2019) — both figures cited, no conflict resolved

911 GT2 RS 'Weissach' Package and the Manthey Performance kit are options, not variants: the Weissach Package was an $18,000 option on the GT2 RS (RM Sotheby's, 2019 GT2 RS 'Weissach' lot, Miami 2025), so the car is modelled once, as 991/gt2-rs; the same is true of the GT3 RS Weissach Package

911 GT3 R (991.2, 2019) and 911 RSR (991-generation) are customer/track racing cars rather than road-legal variants, so neither is modelled here; the chapter's single racing entry, 991/935, is a track-only Porsche-badged special built around the GT2 RS

No 'GT3 RS Heritage' exists: for the 991.2 phase Porsche published only the GT3 RS (2018–2019) and its optional Weissach Package — no Heritage edition was ever announced (checked against the 991 generation article on Wikipedia, 2026-10-03)

911 Carrera Cabriolet / Carrera S Cabriolet / Carrera 4 Cabriolet and the 991.2 Carrera GTS Cabriolet are still unmodelled: they are real road-legal bodies with no roster id and were out of scope for this pass — flagged for a future one
